job.style: a passage that starts from a common wrong idea and corrects it

passage: Many people often confuse weather and climate, thinking they are the same thing, but they are quite different. Weather refers to the day-to-day atmospheric conditions, while climate is the average weather pattern taken over a long period, usually 25 years. For instance, a single cold winter day does not mean the Earth is not warming; it is just a temporary weather event. Similarly, humidity is the amount of water vapour present in the air, and it exists even on dry, sunny days, not just when it is raining. When we look at animal adaptations, we see how specific they are to their environment. Polar bears live exclusively in the Arctic, which is the North Pole, while penguins are found in the Southern Hemisphere. Their white fur is an adaptation for camouflage against the snow, not for trapping extra heat. Furthermore, in a cyclone, the calm, low-pressure centre is called the eye, while the most violent, high-speed winds occur in the region surrounding it. Understanding these distinctions helps us better interpret the natural world around us, moving beyond common myths about how our atmosphere and animal habitats function.

items.evidence: For instance, a single cold winter day does not mean the Earth is not warming; it is just a temporary weather event.
items.q: Last January had one freezing day. What does that day tell us about Earth's warming?
options: It is only a short-term weather event
It proves the Earth is not warming
It shows the climate has turned colder
It means warming happens only in summer
items.explain: One cold day is just temporary weather; it does not mean the Earth is not warming.

wrong.why: thinks a cold winter proves warming is fake
treats one day's weather as climate
over-generalises from a single cold day

items.evidence: Similarly, humidity is the amount of water vapour present in the air, and it exists even on dry, sunny days, not just when it is raining.
items.q: Meena says there is no humidity on a dry, sunny day. What is actually true?
options: The air still holds some water vapour
The air holds water vapour only when raining
The air's humidity equals the day's rainfall
The air is dry, so humidity is zero
items.explain: Humidity is water vapour in the air, and it exists even on dry, sunny days.

wrong.why: thinks humidity exists only during rain
thinks 'dry' means no vapour at all

items.evidence: Their white fur is an adaptation for camouflage against the snow, not for trapping extra heat.
items.q: Why do polar bears have white fur?
options: So they blend in with the snow
So they trap extra heat in the cold
So they match penguins living near them
So they stay cool in warm weather
items.explain: White fur is camouflage that hides polar bears against the snow, not a way to trap heat.

wrong.why: thinks white fur is mainly for warmth
thinks polar bears and penguins share a home
links colour to temperature, not hiding

items.evidence: Furthermore, in a cyclone, the calm, low-pressure centre is called the eye, while the most violent, high-speed winds occur in the region surrounding it.
items.q: A ship sails right into the eye of a cyclone. What will the crew find there?
options: Calm winds and low air pressure
Violent winds at the highest speeds
Strong winds and high air pressure
Calm winds and high air pressure
items.explain: The eye is the calm, low-pressure centre; the most violent winds are in the ring around it.

wrong.why: thinks the eye is the most violent part
thinks fast winds create high pressure
remembers calm but mixes up the pressure
